clue.text: Tongue-tied single, taciturn with ale drunk

parts.note: single is one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A quiet man, made even less talkative by his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the man but is the anagram signal for the two words around 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tongue-tied cannot put words together clearly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Me and mine playing, including son — that's great

indicators.note: including says one piece goes inside the shuffled letters
playing about with the words me and mine shuffles their letters

explanation.surface: Someone delighted that a game involving themselves, their family and their son is going so well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' gives IMMENE, the anagram; 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense and great are synonyms for very large in size.

clue.text: Moving slowly, desperate man's held by stake

indicators.note: held by says the man sits inside the stake

parts.note: an ante is the stake put in before a poker hand
Desperate Dan is the strongman cowboy of the British children's comic The Dandy; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A desperate gambler whose stake is his last hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous strongman from The Dandy, a long-running British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow, walking tempo.

clue.text: Some East-ender is eating mash?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Londoner from the East End tucking into a plate of mash.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: mashing meat softens it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenderise meat is to beat or pound it soft, much as mashing softens food.

clue.text: Vehicle on journey and what it may carry?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a go can mean a trip or turn, as in a go on the roads

explanation.surface: A van on its rounds and the load it carries.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places one piece above the other; the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by a vehicle, ship or plane.

clue.text: Woman having oddly wilder heart, like Bonnie Parker?

indicators.note: having, with heart, says the picked letters form the middle of the woman
heart says the letters sit at the centre of the other word

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of wilder

explanation.surface: A woman with a wild heart, just like the famous outlaw Bonnie Parker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes WLE from WILDER; 'having ... heart' sets it in the middle of LASS. Bonnie Parker was the robber partner of Clyde Barrow in 1930s America.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Parker was a bank robber, an example of an outlaw who ignored the rules.

clue.text: Stand and scold over end of immature adolescent

parts.note: a golf tee is a stand for the ball
to nag is to scold persistently

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of immature

explanation.surface: A parent standing over an immature teenager, scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes someone in their teens, an adjective for the adolescent years.

clue.text: Experienced person if also retrained

indicators.note: retrained suggests the words are put through a new course, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A seasoned worker being sent back for further training.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional approach is expert and seasoned, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Raced around first man returning fast time

indicators.note: around says the raced word wraps the other piece

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, meaning raced

indicators.note: returning means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: A runner who raced round to beat the first man and post a fast time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives MADA; 'fast' means abstaining from food, not speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daytime fasting, so a period of abstinence.

clue.text: Lessen warmth holding back chill

indicators.note: back says those letters are read in reverse
holding says the two words contain the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Turning down the heating, which brings back a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds SSENWAR in lesSEN WARmth; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness of weather is its cold, damp bite, a sense of chilliness.

clue.text: Tests, assuming one works, all right

indicators.note: assuming in its sense of taking on means the tests take in the one

parts.note: SATs are standardised school tests
one is the Roman numeral I
a factory is a works, a manufacturing plant

explanation.surface: Checking that everything is fine, provided the machines function.
explanation.walkthrough: SATs are national school tests in Britain; I goes inside to give SATIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory and all right both mean acceptable, good enough.

clue.text: Intended to purchase new investment

indicators.note: to purchase means to take in, so the betrothed takes in the letter

parts.note: one's intended is one's betrothed, a fiancé

explanation.surface: A plan to buy something new as an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a verb meaning planned, but is the noun for a betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is money supplied for a venture, the capital put in.

clue.text: About repulsed cutting open ham

indicators.note: cutting says the reversed letters slice into the other word

parts.note: overt means open, done publicly

indicators.note: repulsed, driven back, says the abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone driven back while slicing open a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns CA into AC, which cuts OVERT as OVER-AC-T.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated theatricality, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Scandinavian with Estonia due east initially

definitions.text: Scandinavian with Estonia due east initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word before it

explanation.surface: A Nordic person whose neighbour Estonia lies directly to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of all five words spell the answer, and the whole clue is a fair description: Estonia does lie east of Sweden across the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, a Scandinavian country lying west of Estonia.

clue.text: They pretend this compiler's puzzle's taking time

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened to I'm

indicators.note: taking says the puzzles take in another letter

parts.note: a poser is a puzzle; poser's read as plural posers

explanation.surface: The setter boasting that the puzzle takes some time to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPOSTERS is a recognised variant spelling of impostors.
explanation.definitionFit: Impostors are people who pretend to be someone else, fakes.

clue.text: Sovereign head consuming ordinary wine

indicators.note: consuming says the head swallows the other letters

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A monarch's head drinking ordinary wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old crossword favourite, a dark red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a ruler with great power, as a sovereign is.

clue.text: Unwise being saucy embracing Romeo

indicators.note: embracing says the cheeky word hugs the letter

parts.note: saucy means cheeky or impudent
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Getting cheeky while embracing a lover called Romeo is unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking care or good judgment, so unwise.

clue.text: Trek with donkey covered by sheet

indicators.note: covered by says the animal sits inside the sheet

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A long journey with a donkey wrapped in a sheet against the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey, especially a long voyage, so a trek.

clue.text: Lift adulation supporting United

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting below, holding up the letter above

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
praise is adulation, admiration

explanation.surface: Fans' adulation lifting a United side they support.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to raise up, an old verb for lifting.

clue.text: Piano seen in old time musical drama

indicators.note: seen in says this letter appears inside the other pieces

parts.note: an era is a period of time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano seen in a period musical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and sung.

clue.text: Offensive bad smell's revolting prospect

indicators.note: revolting, turning over, says the smell is reversed

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a bad smell; the 's reads as 'is'
a scene is a view or prospect

explanation.surface: A bad smell making the outlook truly revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like the definition, but it turns BO into OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene and offensive both describe something grossly indecent or repugnant.

clue.text: Laments idea regularly adopted by European members

indicators.note: adopted by says the picked letters are taken in by the other pieces

parts.note: legs are limbs, or members

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of idea

explanation.surface: An idea taken up by European parliament members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives IE, the first and third letters of IDEA; it goes inside E-LEGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegies are mournful poems or songs, laments for the dead.

clue.text: 'Cure' play after playing in comeback

indicators.note: after says the play comes after the other piece
in comeback says the word is reversed

parts.note: on means playing, as in a show that is on
to strum is to play a guitar

explanation.surface: A play put on to help an actor's return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in comeback' gives NO. The quote marks on 'Cure' suggest a dubious remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine, a supposed cure of doubtful value.

clue.text: Power of fighter hurt, gutted

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of hurt, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: The strength of a boxer who has been hurt badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighter' suggests a boxer but is the MiG jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Might and power are synonyms for strength or force.

clue.text: Developing source of aroma in name perfume

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of aroma

explanation.surface: A perfumer creating a new scent with a named aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, still emerging.

clue.text: Weeping, the French ruler cradles Antoinette's head

indicators.note: cradles says the other pieces hold this letter between them

parts.note: le is French for the
a king is a ruler

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of the queen's name

explanation.surface: The French king tearfully cradling Marie Antoinette's severed head.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Antoinette was the queen of Louis XVI, guillotined in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaking lets liquid escape, as a weeping wound or pipe does.

clue.text: Studio fed fiction before actor's finale

parts.note: ate means fed, took food
a lie is a fiction, an untruth

indicators.note: finale takes the last letter of actor

explanation.surface: A studio fed a made-up story before an actor's big final scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop.

clue.text: Still, overturned stable roughly shelters

indicators.note: overturned says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: even means steady or stable

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are thrown loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: A stable knocked over, leaving only rough shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horse's building but means steady: EVEN, reversed by 'overturned' to NEVE. 'roughly' rearranges SHELTERS into RTHELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and nevertheless are both adverbs meaning in spite of that.
